arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# The backup destination is intentionally not hard-coded in this repo.
# Supply it as the first argument or via BACKUP_DEST, for example:
#   ./backup.sh /mnt/backups
#   BACKUP_DEST=user@host:/path/to/backups ./backup.sh
DEST="${1:-${BACKUP_DEST:-}}"

if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup destination required" >&2
    echo "usage: $0 <mount-or-local-path|host:path>" >&2
    echo "       BACKUP_DEST=<destination> $0" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Run from the script's directory so relative paths (logs/, tarball) are
# stable no matter where cron or an operator starts the script.
SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote destination (for example user@host:/path/to/backups).
        scp -q "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # Local directory or mounted backup volume.
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
set -eu
DEST_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
cd /tmp
./work/backup.sh "$DEST_DIR"
ls -l "$DEST_DIR"
ls -l work/logs-*.tar.gz
rm -rf "$DEST_DIR" work/logs-*.tar.gz
